samples.text:
The bar chart shows the number of undergraduate and postgraduate students in a university between 2019 and 2025. The pie charts show where the students come from in 2019 and 2025.

Overall, the number of students increased in both group, and the percentage of international students become bigger.

In 2019 there were 14.5 thousand undergraduate students. This number increased to 15.2 thousand in 2021 and 15.8 thousand in 2023, and in 2025 it was 16.1 thousand. The postgraduate students were much less, but they grew faster. They were 3.2 thousand in 2019, then 3.9 thousand in 2021, 5.1 thousand in 2023 and 6.4 thousand in 2025. So the number of postgraduate students doubled.

Looking at the pie charts, in 2019 more than half of the students came from home region (55%), 30% came from other regions and 15% were international. In 2025 the home region students decreased to 44% and other regions decreased a little to 28%. However, international students increased to 28%, which is the same like other regions.
samples.why: Overview present but basic · all data covered accurately, though listed year by year · simple linking (Then, So, However) · repetitive vocabulary (increased, decreased) · several errors in tense, articles and word choice.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares the numbers of undergraduate and postgraduate students at a university from 2019 to 2025, while the two pie charts show where the students came from in 2019 and 2025.

Overall, student numbers rose in both categories, with postgraduate enrolment growing much more rapidly. In addition, the university became considerably more international, although students from home region still formed the largest group.

Undergraduates made up the vast majority of students throughout the period. Their numbers increased gradually from 14.5 thousand in 2019 to 16.1 thousand in 2025. Postgraduate numbers were far lower but rose at a much faster rate, from 3.2 thousand to 3.9 thousand in 2021 and then to 5.1 thousand in 2023, before reaching 6.4 thousand in 2025, which is exactly twice the original figure.

Regarding origin, 55% of students came from the home region in 2019, but this proportion fell to 44% in 2025. The share from other regions was fairly stable, dropping only from 30% to 28%. The most significant change was in international students, whose share almost doubled from 15% to 28%, so that by 2025 they was as numerous as students from other regions.
samples.why: Clear overview covering all three visuals · key contrasts highlighted (growth rates, rising international share) · good cohesion · appropriate less common vocabulary (enrolment) · a couple of minor grammatical slips.

samples.text:
The bar chart presents undergraduate and postgraduate enrolment at a university between 2019 and 2025, and the pie charts break down the student body by place of origin in the first and last of those years.

The university expanded over the six years, largely because of a surge in postgraduate numbers, and its intake became markedly more international, even though students from the home region remained the single largest group.

Undergraduates vastly outnumbered postgraduates throughout, but their numbers grew only modestly, from 14.5 thousand to 16.1 thousand. Postgraduate enrolment, by contrast, rose at an accelerating pace, from 3.2 thousand in 2019 to 5.1 thousand in 2023 and 6.4 thousand in 2025, precisely double its starting level. As a result, the total number of students increased from 17.7 thousand to 22.5 thousand.

The make-up of the student body also changed considerably. In 2019, over half of all students (55%) came from the university's home region, while 30% were from other regions and only 15% from overseas. By 2025, the home-region share had contracted to 44%, and that of other regions had edged down to 28%. International students, meanwhile, had almost doubled their share to 28%, drawing level with those from other regions.
samples.why: Perceptive overview linking growth and origin · figures selected and combined skilfully (totals, doubling) · cohesion seamless · precise vocabulary (make-up, contracted, drawing level) · wide range of error-free structures.
